long_biography.plain_text:
Carling Technologies was already a family enterprise when Richard Wesley Sorenson Sr. joined in 1969. Six years later he succeeded his father, Wesley Sorenson, as president. He paired stewardship with technical participation, working as an inventor on electrical-switch and circuit-breaker designs and tying his leadership to the products rather than only the boardroom.

Under Sorenson, Carling grew into a global manufacturer of switching, circuit-protection and power-distribution systems serving transportation, marine and communications markets. The company acquired marine-electronics specialist Maretron, expanded its engineering and production footprint, and ultimately agreed to join Littelfuse. That transaction closed in November 2021, ending Carling's long period of family ownership. The sale marked the culmination of more than four decades in which Sorenson moved from family successor to the company's president and chief executive.
